memory_update.text: CEG is the clearest direct public-market asset-owner candidate for nuclear restart execution tied to AI/data-center power demand because of the Microsoft-backed Crane Clean Energy Center / Three Mile Island Unit 1 restart.
LEU should remain a high-priority fuel chokepoint candidate because domestic HALEU enrichment capacity is repeatedly cited as a gating item for advanced reactor deployment.
BWXT is a high-quality picks-and-shovels candidate for nuclear-grade components and advanced fuel fabrication; likely less binary than reactor pure plays but requires revenue-materiality checks.

GEV maps to both SMR platform leadership through GE Vernova Hitachi BWRX-300 and second-order grid/power-equipment bottlenecks; nuclear segment materiality should be checked before ranking it against pure plays.
SMR is an obvious public SMR product-leader candidate but should be labeled higher risk until binding customer, financing, EPC, and construction milestones improve.
CCJ was not included due to the five-candidate cap, but Cameco remains a strong next-pass candidate for uranium mining, conversion/fuel services, and Westinghouse exposure.

OKLO was not included in the five-candidate list because this pass prioritized operating assets, fuel, components, and established SMR platforms; however, DOE Reactor Pilot Program participation makes OKLO a necessary high-risk reactor-developer follow-up.

For this node, separate operating nuclear assets and fuel/component bottlenecks from reactor concept announcements; the strongest Serenity evidence will be PPAs, NRC/DOE milestones, production volumes, binding orders, and financed construction rather than press-release pipelines.
Add VST as a high-priority operating-nuclear/data-center PPA candidate; it provides near-term licensed nuclear capacity exposure distinct from SMR concept risk.
Add OKLO as a direct but high-risk advanced nuclear candidate; track fuel access, NRC progress, DOE pilot milestones, financing, and binding offtake quality before upgrading.
Add CW and FLS as nuclear-qualified component and equipment vendors that may benefit from restarts, uprates, SMRs, and new builds; nuclear revenue materiality still needs confirmation.

Add UUUU as a domestic uranium-feedstock candidate; exposure is upstream and indirect to AI data-center power, so evidence should focus on utility contracts, production ramp, and U.S. fuel-security policy.

Further Layer 1B work should test additional US-listed or ADR suppliers in EPC, nuclear engineering software, uranium conversion/enrichment, reactor instrumentation, heavy forgings, grid interconnection, and nuclear waste/logistics.

Add XE as a newly US-listed advanced reactor and fuel platform; it may be more relevant than some older SMR concept equities because Amazon-backed demand and TRISO fuel exposure create a clearer chokepoint mapping, but binding customer-contract quality still needs verification.

Add OKLO as direct DOE Reactor Pilot Program/public advanced reactor exposure; classify as high-upside but high-falsification-risk because revenue, licensing, fuel, and commercial-power delivery remain unproven.
Add VST as operating nuclear-asset exposure; existing nuclear generation may be a more immediately monetizable AI-power bottleneck than SMR announcements.

Add CW as a nuclear-grade component supplier to monitor. Component qualification and limited supplier depth could become a hidden bottleneck if reactor restart, AP1000, SMR, or Gen-IV programs accelerate.

Add UEC as upstream domestic uranium/fuel-security exposure, but do not confuse uranium mining with HALEU enrichment. Its relevance depends on actual production, domestic supply-chain premiums, and downstream conversion/refining progress.

EPC and nuclear engineering exposure remains under-covered after this pass. Jacobs, AECOM, Fluor, and specialty construction/electrical contractors should be checked in a separate pass for nuclear restart/SMR execution capacity, but evidence needs project-level revenue linkage.

node: Firm power, nuclear restarts, SMRs, advanced reactors, and nuclear fuel
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe for the nuclear firm-power node. Highest-relevance candidates cluster around operating nuclear assets and restart execution, domestic HALEU/enrichment, nuclear-grade components and fuel fabrication, SMR/platform technology with regulatory milestones, and incumbent power-equipment platforms. This pass intentionally favors direct exposure over broader AI/data-center beneficiaries and does not provide trading recommendations. Expanded universe focuses on execution chokepoints rather than reactor concept headlines: operating nuclear assets with hyperscaler PPAs, advanced-reactor developers with fuel/regulatory risk, nuclear-qualified components, pumps/valves, and domestic uranium feedstock. The strongest near-node additions are Vistra for operating nuclear power contracted to Meta, Oklo for advanced nuclear/data-center commercialization but high regulatory/fuel risk, Curtiss-Wright and Flowserve as nuclear-grade component suppliers, and Energy Fuels as a U.S. uranium feedstock supplier. Expanded the US-listed universe around the nuclear firm-power chokepoint beyond the seed list. The strongest additions are not just reactor-concept equities; they map to five execution layers: newly public advanced reactor/fuel platform exposure, operating nuclear generation with hyperscaler PPAs, nuclear-grade components, and domestic uranium supply. Key separation criterion: favor companies with operating assets, public counterparties, DOE/NRC milestones, fuel-chain assets, or qualified component positions over pure narrative exposure.
